limits: A browser restart was simulated with a new tab in the same browser profile (sessionStorage gone, localStorage and the IndexedDB sign-in kept); a real Android phone and iPhone restart remains for the owner.
Online flows ran against the local Firebase emulators under a demo project, not the live project.
The 10-minute and 24-hour rules were tested by ageing the saved timestamps, not by waiting.
The Getting back into your game panel shows for about 0.3 s on this PC; it was not captured on slow networks.
Touch was emulated (Chromium hasTouch at 390x844). No screen reader was used.
Performance was not measured in this run (separate /benchmark).

learning.hypothesis: Home and the local Continue card load cleanly on the production build with the new start-up step (6/6, no console errors), so the baseline holds. The change is rejoining online rooms: run the two-browser rejoin suite on the emulators (C1-C4): saving on create and join, host and guest reloads and a browser restart back in the same seat within 3 s, Leave and a closed room clearing the save, That game has ended for a gone room or a lost seat, the 10-minute and 24-hour rules, rematch, and invite links.

Every rejoin contract held (22/22): the host was back in the same seat 443 ms after a reload, guest reload and restart rejoined, closed or lost rooms said so and were forgotten, and the 10-minute and 24-hour rules worked. The same Online screen also runs presence from R1b-1, and rejoin now calls joinPresence again on start-up, so re-run the presence flow (C5) to make sure dropped connections, the away note and offline moves still behave.

Presence is intact on this build (20/20). The one remaining risk is adjacent: App.svelte now decides between reopening an AI game, rejoining an online room and Home at start-up, and probe 001 only covered Home. Re-run the full local-game suite on the production build (C6): reload and restart resume, Continue and Discard, Quit and Restart, pass-and-play on a touch phone, resumed scoring.
